title: Don’t be data poor — Anuj Iravane, Anterior
talk_summary: Anuj Iravane describes how Anterior generates synthetic healthcare records by reversing the inference workflow: sample a label and a reasoning trace from an explicit symbolic policy (decision tree), then generate data backwards conditioned on that trace. The pipeline is a coarse-to-fine, skill-based agent workflow (patient invariants → journey → per-encounter document plans → parallel document generation → eval/refinement loop) that domain experts own and steer, yielding ~90% synthetic datasets and clinicians distinguishing synthetic from real only ~60% of the time.

takeaways.technique: Reverse the inference workflow to generate labeled eval data
takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of labeling real data, they sample a label and a reasoning trace first, then generate the input data conditioned on it, so labels are correct by construction and rare edge cases can be synthesized on demand.
takeaways.evidence_quote: can we actually sort by sampling a random label um figuring out a reasoning trace for that label and then trying to generate data backwards from that
takeaways.numbers: ~90% of datasets are synthetic; blind review clinicians distinguished synthetic from real only ~60% of the time

takeaways.technique: Skills as the interface between engineers and domain experts
takeaways.what_they_do: Every pipeline stage is a skill file running on a generic agent harness, so a domain expert can add a new document type or stage by writing a skill file with no engineering changes.
takeaways.evidence_quote: they could easily just make a new skill file for it, uh attach it to the pipeline, um and and and voila, there wouldn't be any engineering changes required

takeaways.technique: Coarse-to-fine layered generation to keep prompts token-efficient
takeaways.what_they_do: They generate invariants, then a high-level journey, then per-encounter document plans, then fan out to generate documents, keeping each prompt payload small and allowing scaling to long outputs without overloading context windows.
takeaways.evidence_quote: this course to fine layering uh is actually what allows us to keep uh the different prompt payloads in the pipeline very token efficient

takeaways.technique: Eval/refinement loop over parallel fan-out outputs
takeaways.what_they_do: After parallel independent generation, an LLM consistency eval checks for contradictions across documents and feeds back to fix specific parts, plus a roundtrip check that generated data still matches the original label.
takeaways.evidence_quote: one of the eval is an LLM based check for consistency um between all documents. So this makes sure that there's no contradictions

takeaways.technique: Just-in-time synthetic scenarios to pre-test before go-live
takeaways.what_they_do: Because data can be generated from scratch quickly, they model edge cases and simulate them to test workflows before production rather than waiting for customer data.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you kind of just model all your edge cases, simulate them and test your workflows before you go live

takeaways.technique: Explicit symbolic policy representation for deterministic sampling
takeaways.what_they_do: They model policies explicitly as decision trees/symbolic representations, which improves accuracy and consistency and lets them deterministically sample diverse reasoning traces.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we spend a lot of time and energy in trying to model these policies explicitly as decision trees
